```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# ===========================================================================
# DATA
# ===========================================================================

# Veraset profile: one row per county per band. `share` sums to 1 over all 11
# bands; `n_devices` is constant within a county.
profile <- read_csv(PROFILE_CLEAN, col_types = cols(home_county = col_character())) |>
  mutate(home_county = pad_fips(home_county))

# Existing fits, for comparing against anything you refit.
ver_params <- read_csv(VERASET_PARAMS, col_types = cols(home_county = col_character())) |>
  mutate(fips = pad_fips(home_county))

meta_params <- read_csv(META_PARAMS, col_types = cols(fips = col_character())) |>
  mutate(fips = pad_fips(fips))

xwalk <- read_csv(XWALK, col_types = cols(fips = col_character())) |>
  mutate(fips = pad_fips(fips)) |>
  distinct(gid_2, fips)

# Meta's four categories, averaged over the two-week periods, one row per
# county. o1/o2/o3 are the folded shares: the home tile goes into (0, 10).
meta_shares <- read_csv(META_MD, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  inner_join(xwalk, by = join_by(gadm_id == gid_2)) |>
  group_by(fips, ds) |>
  filter(n() == 4) |>
  mutate(frac = distance_category_ping_fraction /
           sum(distance_category_ping_fraction, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  group_by(fips, home_to_ping_distance_category) |>
  summarise(frac = mean(frac, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = home_to_ping_distance_category, values_from = frac) |>
  rename(f0 = `0`, g1 = `(0, 10)`, g2 = `[10, 100)`, g3 = `100+`) |>
  drop_na(f0, g1, g2, g3) |>
  mutate(o1 = f0 + g1, o2 = g2, o3 = g3)


profile  %>%
  summarise(tot = length(unique(home_county))) #good

# ---- two small helpers for pulling one county out -------------------------

# Veraset bands for one county, in the shape every fitting function wants:
# edge_low, edge_high, w (summing to 1), n_devices. Truncated at TRUNC_KM.
veraset_bands <- function(f) {
  profile |>
    filter(home_county == pad_fips(f), edge_high <= TRUNC_KM) |>
    arrange(band_idx) |>
    transmute(edge_low, edge_high, w = share / sum(share), n_devices)
}

veraset_bands(36061)


# Meta's three folded categories for one county, same shape.
meta_bands <- function(f) {
  r <- meta_shares |> filter(fips == pad_fips(f))
  tibble(edge_low  = c(0, 10, 100),
         edge_high = c(10, 100, Inf),
         w         = c(r$o1, r$o2, r$o3))
}

meta_bands
```


```{r setup, include=FALSE}
LA <- "06037"      # big, dense, well sampled
WIBAUX <- "30109"  # tiny, rural, thin panel


# ===========================================================================
# CHEAT SHEET
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What each function is for, and a line you can run.
# ===========================================================================

#   ln_surv(d, mu, sigma)
#   Probability a displacement exceeds d km. S(0) = 1, S(Inf) = 0.
#   ln_surv(c(0, 1, 10, 100), mu = -1.2, sigma = 3.1)

# ln_cdf(d, mu, sigma)
#   The other side: probability of being within d km. The sanity check on any
#   Meta fit is that ln_cdf(10, ...) lands near 0.8.
#   ln_cdf(10, meta_params$mu[1], exp(meta_params$log_sigma[1]))

# ln_cdf_trunc(d, mu, sigma, lo, hi)
#   The CDF renormalised over [lo, hi]. This is what the flow allocation
#   uses, so both sources spread over identical support.
#   ln_cdf_trunc(100, -1.2, 3.1, lo = 0, hi = 500)

# predict_bands(mu, sigma, edge_low, edge_high)
#   Band probabilities under a kernel, renormalised over the bands given.
#   Compare against observed shares to see where a fit misses.
#   b <- veraset_bands(LA)
#   tibble(band = b$edge_low, obs = b$w,
#          fit = predict_bands(-1.2, 3.1, b$edge_low, b$edge_high))

# tv_distance(w, q)
#   Share of probability mass sitting in the wrong band. 0.042 is the
#   lognormal's national median; 0.081 was the two-exponential's.
#   tv_distance(b$w, predict_bands(-1.2, 3.1, b$edge_low, b$edge_high))

# ln_nll(par, bands, n)
#   The objective itself, par = c(mu, log_sigma). Rarely called directly;
#   useful for checking a surface is smooth where you think it is.
#   ln_nll(c(-1.2, log(3.1)), b, n = 50000)

# ln_closed_form(o1, o2)
#   Meta's two-parameter kernel straight from its first two shares. No
#   optimiser: three categories pin exactly two numbers.
#   r <- meta_shares |> filter(fips == LA); ln_closed_form(r$o1, r$o2)

# fit_lognormal(bands, n_starts, seed)
#   Bounded multi-start fit, for the Veraset side. Returns mu, sigma, tv,
#   at_bound, spread, n_starts_ok. Check at_bound before believing anything.
#   fit_lognormal(veraset_bands(LA), seed = 1)
#   fit_lognormal(veraset_bands(WIBAUX), seed = 1)   # thin panel, may bound

# fit_lognormal_hessian(bands, n)
#   Same likelihood with the Hessian kept, for the Meta side. The cov_*
#   columns scale as 1/n and n is made up, so treat them as indicative.
#   fit_lognormal_hessian(meta_bands(LA))

# pad_fips(x) / county_of_cbg(x) / hav_km(lon0, lat0, lon, lat)
#   Keys and distance. pad_fips before every join.
#   hav_km(-118.24, 34.05, -122.42, 37.77)   # LA to SF, expect ~559 km


# ===========================================================================
# THREE COMPARISONS WORTH HAVING OPEN
# ===========================================================================

# 1. Does the new fitter reproduce the old parameters?
fit_lognormal(veraset_bands(LA), seed = 1) # agrees to many decimals
ver_params |> filter(fips == LA, scope == "all") |> select(mu, sigma, tv)

```


```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# 2. Does the closed form agree with the stored Meta fit?
r <- meta_shares |> filter(fips == LA)
ln_closed_form(r$o1, r$o2)
meta_params |> filter(fips == LA) |> mutate(sigma = exp(log_sigma))

meta_pararms <- meta_params %>%
mutate(sigma = exp(log_sigma))

# 3. Where does Meta's kernel miss Veraset's bands?
b <- veraset_bands(LA)
m <- meta_params |> filter(fips == LA)
tibble(lo = b$edge_low, obs = b$w,
           meta = predict_bands(m$mu, exp(m$log_sigma), b$edge_low, b$edge_high)) |>
      mutate(gap = meta - obs)
    # expect most of the disagreement below 10 km, which is the range Meta's
#    # (0, 10) category cannot constrain


meta_shares_new <- meta_shares %>%
  mutate(parms = ln_closed_form(o1, o2)) %>%
  unnest(parms) %>%
  mutate(mu_2 = mu,
         sigma_2 = sigma) %>%
  select(mu_2, sigma_2, fips) %>%
  left_join(meta_params, by = "fips")

meta_shares_new

meta_shares_new %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  mutate(diff_sigma = sigma_2 - exp(log_sigma)) %>%#,
      #      diff_sigma = sigma_2 - sigma) %>%
  filter(diff_sigma > .05) #| sigma_mu > .05)
#we are in business

newly_generated <- read_csv(META_SHARES_FILE)

old
newly_generated %>%

  select("o1.x", "o2.x", "o1.y", "o2.y") %>%

new <- read_csv("E:/dewey-june2025/kernel/trackB/meta_lognormal_kernel-fit.csv.new")
old <- read_csv("E:/dewey-june2025/kernel/trackB/meta_lognormal_kernel-fit.csv")

new %>%
  left_join(old, by = "fips") %>%
  select(mu.x, log_sigma.x, mu.y, log_sigma.y) %>%
  mutate(diff_mu = mu.x - mu.y,
         diff_sigma = log_sigma.x - log_sigma.y) %>%
  filter(diff_mu > 0.1 | diff_sigma > .1) # good here
```
